sources.citation: Wangka Maya Pilbara Aboriginal Language Centre. 'Yinhawangka' language page, wangkamaya.org.au (accessed 2026-09-17).
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing. States a draft Dictionary and Topical Wordlist was produced in 2008, a full Yinhawangka Dictionary is planned for 2026, and a children's book (2014) exists; recordings by Tindale 1957, Holmer 1963, Brand(enstein) 1968, Brown 1979.
Gives phoneme inventory only (6 stops, 6 nasals, 4 laterals, tap, 3 glides; i a u with length) citing Jones 2008; no stress statement.

People who have worked intensively to record the language: No one'; spelling 'same system as is used for Banyjima'; materials = Florey 1982 fieldnotes, Thieberger & Smith 1986 fieldnotes/tapes, von Brandenstein 1968c interim report (AIATSIS PMS 2127) with 'Yinhawangka (Ninanu), brief notes on grammar'.

sources.citation: Sharp, Janet & Nicholas Thieberger. 1992. Bilybara: the Aboriginal languages of the Pilbara region of Western Australia. Port Hedland: Wangka Maya Pilbara Aboriginal Language Centre. 158 pp.

sources.note: Austlang (after Dixon 2002) notes Dench 1991 treats Yinhawangka as possibly a Panyjima dialect, and Jones & Denniss 2008 call the described variety 'very similar to Banyjima'; Dench's Panyjima phonology gives the nearest first-hand stress rule and may comment on Yinhawangka.
